inventoryScope: Registered providers in this process, including enabled installed plugins. Routes are authorable document versions, not additional applications. Executable installations were not probed.

rubric.status: subjective editorial estimates; rounded to five percentage points

coverage.meaning: Estimated breadth of useful application functionality expressible through all assessed routes, against the named functional families; not native API enumeration.

anchors.25: A few useful workflow families, with major application areas missing.
anchors.50: Several central families, with substantial gaps.
anchors.75: Most central workflows, with specialist gaps.
anchors.100: Essentially complete useful application breadth; requires exceptional justification.

abstraction.meaning: How well the supported workflows express user intent and decisions rather than native procedural details. This denominator is the explicitly named supported slice, not the whole application.

anchors.0: Raw native procedures and configuration dominate.
anchors.25: Thin typed wrappers; users assemble most domain decisions.
anchors.50: Reusable domain operations with explicit units and constraints; substantial manual composition.
anchors.75: Workflow intent, defaults, requirements and useful deliverables; some native detail remains.
anchors.100: Complete supported task intent with coherent decisions and handoffs; no material native plumbing exposed.

rubric.comparison: Compare like scopes and rubric versions. Scores are ordinal planning aids, not measured ratios, promises or an overall quality rank. Do not average them across unlike applications.
rubric.independentAxes: Verification confidence, local runtime availability and source-bound qualification are separate readiness facts; tests and operation counts are evidence, not score denominators.
